title: Secure Software Delivery
summary: Verify digests and signatures, review dependency lockfiles, find and rotate leaked secrets, refuse downgrades and build an update client that survives failures.
description: Software is trusted at the moment it is installed, so delivery is where many attacks land. You will check artifact digests, verify an Ed25519-signed release manifest with Go's standard crypto, decide which keys may sign what (and rotate and revoke them), review a synthetic dependency lockfile change for risky edits, scan text for synthetic leaked secrets without echoing them, rotate secrets under a fake clock, and reject replayed or downgraded updates. The capstone is a toy update client that verifies a package, installs it into an A/B slot layout and rolls back, under deterministic failure schedules injected into a simulated disk. Every key, token, package, host and file is fictional and generated by the lessons. Nothing touches the network or a real registry. Assumes Go Practice and Application Security Defence.
outcomes: Verify artifact digests and Ed25519 signatures, parsing only after authenticity is established.
State which key may sign what, and handle expiry, rotation and revocation with an explicit clock.
Review lockfile changes for downgrades, hash swaps, off-policy sources and look-alike names.
Detect leaked synthetic secrets without re-leaking them, and rotate secrets with grace periods and revocation.
Reject replayed, stale and downgraded updates, and install with a commit point so any failure leaves a bootable system.
